cand.title: ESA 2027 Annual Meeting
cand.excerpt: Strong organized hospitality-demand mechanism and confirmed Toronto date; venue commitment reduces current-edition accessibility.

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Primary commercial routing contacts: Christi R. Nam, Director, Meetings and Operations, and Holli Jones, Meetings Manager. The 2027 field-trip guidance requires Christi Nam’s approval for field-trip financial/contractual commitments; it does not establish her exclusive hotel-contract authority. Jennifer Riem supports meeting programming; Wendy Ashburn handles exhibits/sponsorship/advertising; Adrienne Sponberg is Executive Director. Their titles are verified, but Toronto housing procurement ownership is not.
findings.futureEdition: Confirmed upcoming: July 25–30, 2027, Toronto, Ontario, Canada, within the December 2026–June 2028 horizon. ESA identifies it as its 112th Annual Meeting. These are activity dates, not publication dates. The next announced edition after Toronto is August 6–11, 2028, Oregon Convention Center, Portland, Oregon, outside this horizon.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel capacities: the 157-room Radisson cannot house or host the whole convention. ESA reports historical attendance of 4,193 in Portland 2023 and 3,018 in Long Beach 2024; neither is a Toronto forecast. The realistic pitch is an organizer-approved speaker/VIP or delegate sub-block, a university/lab group, or a small business meeting, not exclusive housing. A 15–109 peak-room range is a sales-fit envelope from the brief, not published event demand. The hotel’s official page places it steps from MTCC, supporting urban walkable fit rather than resort displacement. Its notice says “Restaurant and Lounge closed until further notice”; do not sell catering, receptions or food-and-beverage packages without operational confirmation.
findings.venueCommitments: Metro Toronto Convention Centre, 255 Front Street West, Toronto, Ontario M5V 2W6, Canada: Toronto proper, downtown/MTCC territory, not a suburban or resort venue. This is a published meeting-venue commitment, not a competing host-hotel booking. Toronto hotel contracts, room allocations and any MTCC hall/building assignment were not published in the reviewed materials.
findings.historicalRotation: Official editions rotate destinations: Montreal 2022; Portland 2023; Long Beach 2024; Baltimore 2025; Salt Lake City 2026; Toronto 2027; announced Portland 2028. Recurrence is verified by edition listings, but annual recurrence does not mean annual Toronto demand. The past-meetings archive has a year typo under 2024; the contemporaneous 2024 media advisory establishes August 4–9, 2024.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Toronto 2027: no edition-specific official hotel list, room-block inventory, housing agency, reservation-opening date or open lodging RFP was located on the reviewed official pages as of November 15, 2026. Therefore every published Toronto hotel name cannot be enumerated: none was found, which is not proof that no contracts exist. ESA general policy says city bids include “the rates for booking a hotel block for attendees” and “we guarantee the booking and use of thousands of hotel room nights at contracted hotels.” This is general policy, not a Toronto room-night figure. Historical 2026 evidence: “Book your hotel room reservation through ESA’s official housing bureau, Orchid, to secure discounted rates!” That page lists Salt Lake Marriott Downtown at City Creek and Hilton Salt Lake City Center, both historical incumbents only. Orchid is not verified for 2027.
findings.organizationStructure: ESA is a nonpartisan, nonprofit scientific association, not a hotel, corporate event owner, PCO or DMC. Its staff directory includes an internal Meetings and Operations team. The Meetings Committee oversees site selection; staff evaluate finalists and recommendations go to the Governing Board. No Toronto-specific external PCO/DMC or housing bureau was established. Orchid is documented only for the 2026 housing pathway.
findings.competitiveLimitations: ESA warns that bookings outside its official block can prevent it meeting contractual room-night minimums and trigger financial penalties. This limits an unaffiliated out-of-block sales strategy. No Toronto incumbent hotels, sell-out, waitlist, inventory shortage, room-night minimum or actual overflow requirement was verified. The 2026 hotels and Orchid relationship cannot be promoted to Toronto commitments. The hotel’s restaurant/lounge closure is a separate execution constraint.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact Christi Nam and Holli Jones through their official staff-directory addresses now. Ask who controls Toronto housing, whether a bureau/official block has been appointed, whether supplemental hotel proposals are accepted, and what dates, rate limits, commission terms and pickup expectations apply. Offer a small conditional sub-block within the supplied 15–109-room sales envelope only after hotel inventory review; do not quote that range as event demand. Ask about speaker/VIP and affiliated-group needs. Revisit ancillary meetings when social-event requests open in late January 2027; verify restaurant/lounge and banquet operations before any catered offer. If 2027 is fully allocated, request approved overflow criteria and relationship development for a future Toronto cycle, not an invented future tender.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: For the 2027 target, meeting venue access is already committed to MTCC; hotel sourcing remains unconfirmed, not demonstrably open and not demonstrably closed. The seed status likely_closed_incumbent is not substantiated for lodging by the venue alone. Seek inclusion in the official accommodation pathway or approved supplemental demand before pricing. Social/business events can be outside the main venue; the authoritative Important Dates page schedules social-event requests for late January 2027 with April 15, 2027 deadline. Session Types contains an apparent stale 2017 deadline; do not use it as the 2027 deadline.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: prioritize 2027 supplemental housing eligibility while developing an ESA meetings-team relationship for any later Toronto return. ESA generally chooses destinations five years ahead; a future Toronto return is not announced. Portland 2028 is officially announced but outside both this hotel’s local territory and the stated horizon; recurrence alone creates no Toronto room demand. Future capture should target early official-block participation, not imply an open RFP or challenge already-announced convention-center commitments.
